en: Wearing shoes with rubber soles increases friction with the ground, helping prevent dangerous slips and falls when walking on wet floors.
Because water conducts electricity, you must never touch electrical switches or unplug appliances with wet hands to avoid severe electric shocks.
Wearing light-colored cotton clothes during sunny days reflects heat away from your body, helping prevent heat exhaustion and sunburns.
Ultraviolet light from the sun can damage your eyes, so wearing sunglasses with UV protection prevents long-term vision problems.
Prolonged exposure to sounds louder than 85 decibels, like loud headphones, can permanently damage the delicate hair cells in your ears.
Using an inclined plane like a ramp to push heavy boxes reduces the lifting force needed, protecting your back from muscle strain.
Strong magnets can interfere with pacemakers and erase magnetic strips on bank cards, so keep them separated from these sensitive devices.
Carrying a heavy backpack on both shoulders keeps your center of gravity balanced, preventing falls and reducing strain on your spine.
Rubbing your hands together converts kinetic energy into thermal energy through friction, which practically warms your skin during cold weather.
Plugging too many appliances into one extension cord overloads the circuit, generating excess heat that can start a dangerous electrical fire.
Wearing clothing with retroreflective strips at night bounces car headlights back to the driver, making you highly visible and preventing accidents.
A sharp knife acts as a better wedge than a dull one, requiring less force to cut food and reducing slipping risks.
